_exec_summary.SummaryText:
OVERVIEW
The Air Liquide commitment to safety and environmental protection for the Air Liquide, El Segundo Hydrogen Facility extends beyond the plant. As part of the community, Air Liquide has a responsibility to our customers, near neighbors and the community at large to help provide a safe working and living environment.  Through safety, concern for the environment, and community involvement, we can develop a true partnership with our customers and community.  

Regulated Chemical and Covered Process 
Air Liquide Large Industries, U.S.  L.P. (Air Liquide) El Segundo Hydrogen facility (Hydrogen Facility) is located within the Chevron El Segundo refinery complex in El Segundo, CA.  The Hydrogen Facility steam methane reforming process is considered the covered process, as defined under the Federal and state accidental release prevention regulations, as a flammable mixture process having an inventory in excess of 10,000 pounds.
 
The Hydrogen Facility steam methane reforming process is designed to provide an efficient production of high purity hydrogen product using refinery and natural gas feedstocks. The hydrogen reforming and purification is performed at elevated pressure. High pressure purified hydrogen is transported to other refinery units via intra refinery pipeline.   The El Segundo Hydrogen Facility is designed for continuous safe operation.

GENERAL ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM STEPS
Air Liquide El Segundo Hydrogen Facility is covered by EPAs accidental release prevention program regulations and is subject to California and Federal accidental release prevention regulations and OSHAs process safety management (PSM) standard.   The Hydrogen Facility steam methane reforming process is closely monitored and controlled to prevent accidental releases to the environment.   Because the process uses and produces flammable gasses, Air Liquide takes safety precautions necessary to prevent human error and reduce potential risks to personnel, the nearby c

ommunity, and the environment. 
Air Liquides policy is to comply with all applicable federal and state rules and regulations. The summary below discusses the process safety system in place to implement the accidental release prevention program.
 
Employee Participation
At the Air Liquide El Segundo Hydrogen Facility, employees are expected to participate in the accidental release prevention program (PSM/RMP).   The specific ways an employee can be involved in the accident prevention program are documented in the Employee Participation plan.  Forms of participation include being part of monthly safety meetings, a PHA, a PSSR, and/or being involved in incident investigation. Employees also participate in the annual review of the covered process operating procedures to ensure the procedures are correct and to recommend any necessary changes. Employees receive training on the Hydrogen Facilitys process safety information and are given access to it.

Process Safety Information (PSI)
Air Liquide keeps a variety of technical documents onsite electronically that are used to help maintain safe operation of its processes.  These documents address chemical properties and associated hazards, equipment design/configuration information, specific chemical inventories and operation limits for key process parameters  all key information for operating the process safely. 
 
Process Hazard Analysis
Air Liquide has a risk management program to help ensure that hazards associated with the various processes are identified and controlled.  The covered process underwent an initial process hazard analysis (PHA) and continues to undergo periodic PHAs and PHA re-validations at least every five years.  The PHA team consists of members with the appropriate experience to define the hazards.  Management reviews the findings and develops a resolution action plan for each item, which is documented, tracked and ultimately closed in the Air Liquide action item tracking system. 
 
Operating Proced

ures
Air Liquide maintains written procedures that address various modes of hydrogen purification process operations, such as (1) unit initial startup; (2) unit normal and temporary operations; (3) unit shutdown; (4) emergency shutdown; (5) startup following an emergency shutdown; and (6) process deviation, consequence and action.  These procedures are used by experienced operators and provide a basis for consistent training of new operators. These procedures are reviewed and annually certified as current and accurate.
 
Training
Air Liquide has implemented a training program for all employees involved in operating the hydrogen purification process.  All employees receive a combination of classroom, computer-based (CBT) and hands-on training that address such topics as: general orientation, site rules and practices, process safety information, normal and emergency operating procedures, health and safety consideration, use of safety procedures and equipment, incident investigation and emergency response.  In addition, all operators are required to attend refresher training at least every three years.  Training is documented and tracked in an electronic learning management system.
 
Contractors
Air Liquide uses outside contractors to support maintenance activities.  Procedures are in place to make sure that contractors perform their work in a safe manner by ensuring they:  (1) have the appropriate knowledge and skills, (2) are aware of the hazards in their workplace, and (3) understand what they should do in the event of an emergency. Safe work practice training is conducted and verified by the Southern California Occupational Safety Council of America. On-site, contractors receive additional information about job hazards through work permit reviews. Contractors are prequalified and periodically re-evaluated to ensure that both their safety performance and training required for work on the Hydrogen Facility covered process are in compliance.

Pre-startup Safety Review

s (PSSRs)
Air Liquide ensures the safety of new/modified facilities or processes before placing those facilities or processes into service through the use of pre-startup safety reviews (PSSRs).  PSSRs are intended to ensure safety through confirmation that:  (1) construction and equipment are in accordance with design specifications; (2) safety, operating, maintenance and emergency procedures are in place and adequate; (3) PHAs have been performed and recommendations resolved before startup of new plants or processes; (4) MOC requirements have been satisfied for modified facilities; and (5) training has been completed for affected employees.

Mechanical Integrity
Air Liquide has established mechanical integrity (MI) practices and procedures, based on preventative philosophy, to maintain pressure vessels, piping systems, relief valves, vent systems, controls, pumps and compressors, and emergency shutdown systems in a safe operating condition.  The basic aspects of this program include: (1) conducting training, (2) developing written procedures, (3) performing inspections and tests; (4) correcting identified deficiencies, and (5) applying quality assurance measures.  In combination, these activities form a system that maintains the mechanical integrity of the process equipment. 
 
The MI program assists with the verification and suitability of new and existing process equipment and, as well as quality control of spare parts and modifications to existing process equipment.
 
Safe & Hot Work Permit System
Air Liquide has a safe & hot work permit system in place to help ensure worker and process safety.  This system is comprised of a group of corporate procedures and standards under the life safety program.  Procedures in place include energy control,  safe work,  hot work, confined space entry and process line break.  Facility personnel are trained in these safe work practices to ensure that operations and maintenance activities are performed safely.

Management of Chan

ge
Air Liquides management of change (MOC) procedure has established the requirements for ensuring that proposed process or equipment changes or changes indirectly affecting processes are evaluated, approved, and documented prior to implementation.  The MOC procedure outlines the requirements for documenting, evaluating the impact, and approving planned changes.  All MOCs are submitted, reviewed by appropriate subject matter specialists (such as Engineering, Risk Management, Operations, Health and Safety), approved, tracked, and closed.  Personnel whose assigned job functions are impacted by the MOC, are briefed and /or trained in the MOC requirements.
 
 Compliance Audits
To help ensure the accident prevention program is functioning properly, Air Liquide conducts an audit to determine whether the procedures and practices required by the accidental release prevention program are being implemented.  Compliance audits are conducted at least every three years.  Resolutions to the recommendations are documented, tracked and closed.
 
Incident Investigation
Air Liquide has implemented incident management procedures that establish the requirements for reporting, investigating and communicating the results of incident investigations.      Air Liquide documents incident and subsequent investigation, follow up actions, and closure.  Results of findings and corrective actions are shared with employees who could be affected by the findings. 

CHEMICAL SPECIFIC PREVENTION STEPS
Air Liquides accidental release prevention program activities      help prevent potential accident scenarios that could be caused by equipment failures and human errors.  The following are examples of the types of safety features in place:
 
	Automated process control shutdowns
	Automatic and manual valves that provide for isolation of the process
	Manual Emergency process shutdowns located in the control room and process area 
	Pressure Safety Relief Valves and Flare system
	Fire water monitor a

nd hydrant system
	Special personal protective equipment (e.g., FRC protective clothing,)
	Personal/portable ambient air monitors
 
 FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
The El Segundo  Hydrogen Facility has had no accidents in the past 5 year that have met the definition of having resulted in death, injuries, or significant property damage on site, or known off-site deaths, injuries, evacuations, sheltering in place, property damage, or environmental damage.
 
EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM INFORMATION
The Air Liquide El Segundo Hydrogen Facility is designated as a non-responding stationary source under EPA RMP regulations.  The facility maintains a written emergency action plan (EAP) which is coordinated with its primary emergency responder, The El Segundo Chevron Refinery Fire Department, and the City of El Segundo Fire Department (the assigned Certified Unified Program Agency or CUPA). In California, most coordination with local emergency response is through the assigned CUPA. Coordination with the LEPC is through an annual electronic submittal.     
           
The El Segundo Hydrogen Facility Emergency Action Plan is reviewed annually, with refresher training provided to ensure ongoing preparedness.  The Hydrogen Facility employees are trained to first responder awareness level to be ready in the event of accidental releases of a regulated substance.   The EAP provides details for emergency health care and the safe evacuation of facility personnel, contractors and visitors.  The EAP describes communicating with Chevron Refinery Fire Department and outside agencies in the event of a loss of containment from the Hydrogen Facility flammable covered process.        
     
PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY
The El Segundo Hydrogen Facility resolves all findings of its PHA and other hazard reviews some of which result in modifications of the process. In 2024, the overpressure relief system that discharges to the flare was improved to decrease the likelihood of atmospheric rele

ases. At this time, all PHA findings are resolved except for one change which requires a major outage to implement. This remaining planned change will implement a low oxygen fuel shutoff to the reformer to prevent the system from becoming fuel rich. The change has been reviewed using management of change and will be implemented at the next planned turnaround in November 2028 or earlier if possible.
In 2020, the Hydrogen Facility disconnected and removed a liquid pentane steam methane reformer feedstock system from service reducing the Hydrogen Facility onsite flammable substance process inventory by 30,000+ pounds.
